text:
Mia: Heads-up: we've got a reproducible 401 flake on Android that only shows up when client uses HTTP/2. Small repro: two signed-in users concurrently hitting /user/profile, ~1% of A's requests 401 while B succeeds.
Sam: Any logs or a minimal repro app? Could be the usual token refresh race.
Mia: Not the classic race. I built a tiny sample that signs in two accounts and issues parallel requests. Repro on emulator API 31 and real Pixel 6 devices. When I force HTTP/1.1 the issue disappears.
Oleg: Interesting. Sounds like connection coalescing/a proxy-level session binding. OkHttp can reuse the same h2 connection across hosts if certs allow; if the proxy binds auth to connection or reuses cached headers, one user's token might be getting applied to another stream.
Katy: How are you toggling h2 in the SDK?
Mia: Quick local workaround:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .protocols(listOf(Protocol.HTTP_1_1))
  .build()
```
Sam: That's a heavy workaround (performance hit). Could we instead always inject Authorization at network-interceptor time, or add Connection: close for problematic endpoints?
Oleg: Note: app interceptors run before connection selection in OkHttp. If token injection happens there it could be captured by the wrong connection. Use a network interceptor to add/refresh Authorization so the header is assembled right before the stream.
Mia: Example network interceptor I used to mitigate the repro:
```kotlin
.addNetworkInterceptor { chain ->
  val token = tokenStore.current()
  val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
    // optional: force per-request connection for buggy proxies
    .header("Connection", "close")
    .build()
  chain.proceed(req)
}
```
Katy: Also make sure our Authenticator that handles 401/refresh is synchronized and updates tokenStore atomically. Two simultaneous refreshes can stomp tokenStore and cause transient 401s.
Sam: FYI emulator & system OkHttp versions differ from our shaded client; some Android images have different default h2 behavior. Add this to troubleshooting notes.
Mia: Pushed a minimal repro and steps to the internal repo: https://git.internal/repro/h2-conn-coalesce (internal). Plan: ship SDK 0.12.5 canary that defaults to HTTP/1.1 on Android while infra investigates proxy behavior. Also add opt-in flag to re-enable h2.
CI-Bot: canary build started: 0.12.5-rc2.
Oleg: Please add a CI integration test in devex/sample-apps: matrix run across http1/h2 on emulator API 28/31 and a physical device lane. Fail when we see interleaved 401s in repro pattern.
Katy: I'll write a short migration note showing the network-interceptor pattern + explanation of connection coalescing. Keep the workaround while backend/edge teams fix proxy binding.
Mia: Logged follow-up issue to track root cause and postmortem. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
